changes.after: An object runs its starting setup from top to bottom when it is created.

before: A primary constructor appears in the class header. Prefixing a parameter with val or var also declares a property. A plain parameter can be used during initialization without becoming a public property.

Property initializers and init blocks run in textual order when constructing an instance. The constructor argument is available to them. Here the two init blocks visibly surround a property initializer; there is no hidden call to start initialization later.

Expected output or behavior: start:Maps
length:4. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Add a third init print and predict its position before running. You may trace it without a Kotlin compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A constructor sets up a new object. Kotlin's primary constructor is written after the class name. Putting val or var before its parameter also creates a stored property. Here, title becomes a property.
Initialization means setting up the starting state. Property starting values and `init` blocks run in their written order. An init block is a group of instructions that runs during this setup.
The screen shows `start:Maps`, then `length:4`. The first init block prints the title. Kotlin then sets length to 4. The second init block reads that length.
Creating the object starts this setup immediately. A constructor parameter without val or var can help with setup, but does not automatically become a property.
